blocks.x: In the words of the antithesis of Mariah Carey, it’s (not) tiiiiiime — not quite yet, anyway! We’re all for spooky season here, and we’re certainly not ones to rush through the seasons, especially when there’s scenic fall foliage to admire, Halloween candy to eat, and cozy sweaters to wear. But New Yorkers know that once October hits, the holiday season has a way of sneaking up on us. And one of the city’s most beloved winter destinations is already getting ready to welcome it back.

In just two weeks, Bryant Park will transform into a full-blown holiday wonderland once again, bringing back its annual Winter Village in the heart of Midtown. The massive seasonal market will fill the park with more than 170 shops, while the centerpiece of the festivities — a giant Christmas tree and the city’s iconic free ice-skating rink — return for another season.

Whether you’re looking to get a head start on holiday shopping, sip something festive while wandering through the market, lace up your skates, or simply soak up some quintessential New York Christmas vibes, Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park is basically the city’s answer to stepping into a holiday movie.

Ryan Muir / Bryant Park
What to See at Bryant Park Bank of America Winter Village

The Rink: A massive 17,000-square-foot ice-skating rink nestled right under the Midtown skyline. It remains New York City’s only free-admission ice skating rink, making it a budget-friendly must-visit for locals and tourists alike.

Holiday Shops by Urbanspace: Over 170 custom-designed “jewel box” kiosks winding along the park’s tree-lined allées and terraces. You’ll find unique gifts, handcrafted jewelry, artwork, and local gourmet provisions from artisans across NYC and around the globe.

The Lodge Bar & Food Hall: An open-air, rinkside après-skate hangout where you can warm up with festive craft cocktails, craft beers, and comfort food dishes from local favorite vendors while watching skaters pass by.

Cozy Igloos: Private, heated transparent domes steps from the ice where parties of up to 8 can enjoy seasonal food spreads and hot drinks in a personal winter bubble. (In early 2027, these undergo a romantic glow-up into “Rosy Igloos” just in time for Valentine’s season)!

Source / Colin Miller via Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park
Free Ice Skating: Hours, Tickets & Tips

Dates & Hours: The Rink runs from October 28, 2026 through February 28, 2027. It is open daily from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM (with extended hours until midnight during peak holiday weeks from Nov 19 – Jan 3).
Admission Cost: Admission is 100% free if you bring your own ice skates!
Skate Rentals: If you don’t own skates, high-quality rental skates are available on-site. Bank of America cardholders receive a 10% discount on skate rentals when booking online.
Reservations: Advance timed-entry ticket reservations are required for all skaters online before heading to the park.

Source / Colin Miller via Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park
Upcoming Events & Seasonal Highlights
Opening Day Extravaganza (Oct 28, 2026): Gates officially open at 12:00 PM on Wednesday, October 28, kicking off four full months of winter festivities.
Live After Dark Series: Look out for live musical performances, DJ sets, and evening skate sessions every night leading up to Christmas Eve (starting Dec 18).
Annual Tree Lighting Ceremony: The village lights up its towering Christmas tree with celebrity performances, synchronized skating shows, and festive fireworks.
When Does It Open?
Mark your calendars! The Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park officially opens on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 12:00 PM.
The Holiday Shops will run daily through January 3, 2027, while The Rink and The Lodge will stay open for winter fun all the way through February 28, 2027.
Don’t miss out! Follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and now on WhatsApp, too!
